title: ephemeral throttle harmonizer and standby drain probe (SLO smoothing + hotfix)
author: Priya N. Rao
ci_status: pass (one flaky integration test retried and green)
release_notes:
- Introduce 'ephemeral throttle harmonizer' to smooth tenant-level admission throttles across regions and reduce oscillation.
- Add 'standby drain probe' to avoid KV cache drain storms during regional failover.
- Fix circuit reopen flapping by adding per-tenant reopen cooldown and enhanced telemetry.
- Backported minimal hotfix to release/* for immediate mitigation of production incidents.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR implements an SLO-focused admission smoothing layer (ephemeral throttle harmonizer) and a small but critical standby drain probe that prevents mass KV cache drains during regional failover. We shipped a small change to circuit reopen logic to stop rapid flip-flops observed under surge conditions (root cause seen in recent incident SUP-3321). Goal is: reduce tenant-level oscillation, protect downstream serving nodes from simultaneous heavy KV work, and provide richer telemetry so on-call can reason about reopen events.

What it changes (high level):
- runtime/admission/harmonizer.go: new SLO-aware harmonizer that aggregates short-term token usage and produces a smoothed per-tenant admission score. Uses exponential smoothing with configurable alpha and a soft cap window; integrates with existing admission API.
- runtime/drain/standby_probe.go: probe that runs during region-standby transitions; verifies KV cache health and delays non-critical drains until probe passes or soft timeout.
- runtime/circuit/reopen_guard.go: per-tenant cooldown (backoff multiplier + jitter) to avoid reopen flapping; records reopen_reason and reopen_attempts into telemetry.
- operator/helm/templates/configmap.yaml: new config knobs to tune harmonizer alpha, probe timeout, and reopen cooldown values.
- tools/eval/promptset_stability.yaml: test harness additions to simulate bursty tenant traffic and verify harmonizer behavior.
- docs/observability/reopen-telemetry.md: docs for the new telemetry fields and alert guidance.
- release/2026-02-hotfix/*: minimal backport for release branch with opt-in flags.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for harmonizer smoothing and timeout behavior.
- [x] Integration scenario in eval harness that reproduces incident-like oscillation and demonstrates improvement.
- [x] Added metrics/traces and dashboard snippets for reopen events.
- [x] Backported opt-in hotfix for release channel and documented escape hatch.
- [x] SRE review and oncall runbook entry drafted.

Review conversation (selected):
- Samir Patel (reviewer): "This addresses the production flip-flop we've seen. Two asks: 1) add a metric for harmonizer smoothing lag so SRE can detect stuck state, 2) ensure probe can't block critical KV drains during progressive rollout."
- Priya (author): "Added harmonizer.smoothing_lag_gauge and a probe fast-path for critical drains (configurable). Both changes are in the last commit a1b2c3d."
- Elena Kirov (reviewer): "Unit tests look good, but the integration harness needs an assertion on request latency tail to ensure we didn't regress P99. Can you add a regression assert?"
- Priya: "Added latency tail assertion in tools/eval/promptset_stability.yaml; CI shows this scenario improves P99. See b2c3d4e."
- Marcus Li (approver): "Read through the helm knobs. Good opt-in defaults. Approving for merge after CI passes. Consider follow-up to expose harmonizer knobs per-tenant via console (tracked ENG-4210)."

CI and rollout notes:
- CI summary: unit (pass), integration (initially failed due to test ordering), integration rerun (pass), lint (pass), e2e (skipped on hotfix backport). One flaky test (tools/eval/promptset_stability) retried once and green.
- Canary plan: staged rollout behind feature flag 'harmonizer.enabled' and 'standby_probe.enabled'. Canary on a small non-critical namespace for 24h, monitor harmonizer.smoothing_lag_gauge, reopened_circuit_count, kv_drain_duration, and request p99. If reopen rate increases unexpectedly, flip feature flag off — the harmonizer is designed as non-blocking and can be toggled without restarts.

Why this is safe as a hotfix:
- The change is opt-in by default (harmonizer.enabled=false in release hotfix), the reopen cooldown only adds a conservative backoff (no functional change unless enabled), and the standby probe defers only non-critical drains behind a soft timeout. The backported patch keeps defaults unchanged and exposes knobs so SRE can enable gradually.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- ENG-4210: Console controls for per-tenant harmonizer tuning and telemetry dashboards.
- ENG-4232: Evaluate cost impact of harmonizer on batching effectiveness and provide guidance in Redwood Optimize.
- Small perf tuning on harmonizer loop to reduce goroutine wakeups; tracked in follow-up branch.

Merge outcome:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Merge commit summary: "squash: introduce ephemeral throttle harmonizer and standby drain probe; reopen cooldown; config knobs; tests; docs"
- Post-merge action: backport applied to release/2026-02-hotfix and flag defaults set to false. Oncall runbook updated under docs/ops/oncall/harmonizer.md.

Telemetry / observability details (quick reference):
- metrics introduced: harmonizer.smoothing_lag_gauge, harmonizer.admission_score, standby_probe.last_pass_timestamp, reopen.cooldown_seconds, reopen.attempts_count
- traces: span names 'harmonizer.evaluate' and 'standby_probe.run' with attributes tenant_id and region
- logs: reopen_reason logged with structured field reopen_reason and reopen_attempts

If there are any concerns about rollout risk or additional telemetry needs we should address them before enabling harmonizer in production namespaces. Overall, this PR is scoped to reduce oscillation during regional load perturbations and to prevent mass KV drains during failover windows while providing SRE with the signals needed to diagnose failures.
notes: Backported opt-in hotfix applied to release/2026-02-hotfix; feature flags default to false for immediate safety; dashboards updated; oncall runbook added.
